turns.text: The previous story examined Hopfield Network. Now the camera turns to Self-organizing Map and a new question along the same timeline: Why did researchers need Self-organizing Map, and where were the existing methods getting stuck?

Teuvo Kohonen introduced self-organizing maps as adaptive networks that arrange output units into topology-preserving maps of input signals. The method made unsupervised competitive learning visible as a two-dimensional grid.
The best-matching unit and its neighbors move toward an input, gradually shaping a topology-preserving map.

Experts generally treat self-organizing maps as a classic unsupervised neural model for visualization and topology preservation. Its long-term legacy is the competitive-learning map, still used to explain clustering, vector quantization, and interpretable low-dimensional organization.
The thread continues with Deep Belief Network, where researchers push the problem one step further.
